note:
**The meaning of the verses**
﴿وَجَاءَ مِنْ أَقْصَى الْمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اتَّبِعُوا الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾
And from a far part of the city a man came hurrying (this was when he learned that the people of the town intended to kill the messengers or torture them). He said: "O my people, follow the messengers sent to you from Allah; follow those who ask you for no money for delivering the message, and who are rightly guided in what they call you to, the worship of Allah alone." This shows the merit of whoever strives to enjoin good and forbid evil.

﴿قِيلَ ادْخُلِ الْجَنَّةَ ۖ قَالَ يَا لَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ ﴿بِمَا غَفَرَ لِي رَبِّي وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ﴾
After he was killed, he was told, "Enter Paradise," as an honour for him. He said, while in bliss and honour: "If only my people knew of my Lord's forgiveness of me and His honouring of me, because of my faith in Allah, my patience in obeying Him, and my following His messengers until I was killed; then they would believe in Allah and enter Paradise like me."

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. The man lived at the far end of the city, far away from the messengers. So why did he come hurrying instead of staying at home?
2. How did he speak to his people? (Gently, and he talked to them about himself: ﴿وَمَا لِيَ لَا أَعْبُدُ الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي﴾ (And why should I not worship the One who created me?), and he did not insult them.)
3. What did he wish for after they killed him and Allah honoured him? Did he hold a grudge against them? And does this mean you should face someone who hurts you alone? (No; you say the truth politely, and if you are afraid of being hurt, you tell the grown-ups.)

**This week's exercise**
If your child sees a friend or a brother or sister doing something wrong this week (cheating in a game, or making fun of someone), they say the word of truth gently as the man did, and then tell you what they said and how they said it.
